---

# ARC: object slides toward a full-width divider

In a demonstrated task family, a full row/column of one color acts as a divider, a compact shape of another color moves toward it along the perpendicular axis, and color 8 marks a trailing boundary row/column.

## Evidence and observed behavior

- Demo with a horizontal color-2 line at row 6: a color-4 shape originally at rows 3–4 moved down one row to rows 4–5, adjacent to the line. The vacated top row (row 3) became all 8s.
- Demo with a horizontal color-2 line at row 10 and a color-3 shape at rows 20–22: the shape moved upward to rows 11–13, adjacent to the line, and row 14 became all 8s.
- Thus preserve shape and divider, slide shape toward the divider until adjacent, and paint the row immediately behind the moved shape (away from the divider) with 8. Preserve other cells/background.

## Procedure

1. Identify the full solid line and its color; identify the separate small shape and its color.
2. Determine the direction toward the line and translate the shape as a rigid object until its nearest occupied cell is adjacent to the line.
3. Paint the full row/column immediately behind the translated shape (on the side away from the divider) color 8, replacing anything there.
4. Keep the grid dimensions and all unrelated cells unchanged. If the geometry/behavior is not fully specified, request a demo rather than guessing.

## Pitfall

The trail is not painted on the divider or at the shape's initial location by default; it is the full line immediately behind the shape after it has moved. In the solved instance where the shape was already adjacent to the divider, the 8 row was immediately above the shape.",
